explanation: I found no Mathlib counterpart, and I don't expect one: the theorem lives entirely in the library's own Navier–Stokes/CKN setup. It says that second spatial derivatives of the vorticity satisfy a heat equation with divergence-form right-hand side. Every object in the statement is defined by the library: `ParabolicPoint`, `unitCylinder`, `IsClassicalSolutionOn`, `curlComp`, `timePartial`, `spatialPartial`, `spatialSecondPartial` and `serrinVortFlux`. The proof uses only library lemmas: `heat_divergence_equation_spatialPartial`, `contDiffOn_spatialPartial`, `contDiffOn_curlComp_unitCylinder`, `contDiffOn_serrinVortFlux` and `vorticity_first_derivative_equation`. Mathlib has no theory of parabolic cylinders, classical Navier–Stokes solutions or vorticity equations, so this is not a duplicate or a special case of anything there. I did not run a name or content search in Mathlib, because none of the statement's constants exist there.
